Article 9
(1) The scope of acts of violence against women and children includes:
a. acts of violence that occur within the household; and
b. acts of violence that occur outside the household.
(2) Acts of violence that occur within the household as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a occur within the household committed by:
a. husband or wife within a marriage;
b. those having blood family relations, marriage, customary relations, adoption; or
c. those working for others or living and residing with others.
(3) Acts of violence that occur outside the household as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b occur outside the household including:
a. harassment;
b. violence discrimination in the workplace;
c. violence in conflict areas;
d. violence in mass media; and
e. human trafficking.

Article 7
Sexual violence as referred to in Article 4 letter c includes acts in the form of:
a. sexual harassment; and/or
b. coercion of sexual relations, in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Bontang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the administration of the Regional Government.
3. Regional Head is the Mayor of Bontang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus of the Bontang City Government.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively, including information services, accompaniment and legal aid, counseling services, medical services, and safe houses through referral.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. General Hospital is a service facility that provides basic and specialist medical services, medical support services, hospital installation/unit services, and care services on an outpatient and inpatient basis.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
10. Services are actions that must be immediately provided to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
11. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy, and advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, as stipulated in a decision of an authorized official.
12. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance for the self-strengthening of victims of domestic violence to resolve the problems faced.
13. Victim Recovery is all actions to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered, both physically and psychologically.
14. Recovery Implementation is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
15. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among recovery implementers in providing services to recover victims of domestic violence.
16. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (domestic helpers, drivers and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
20. Household Scope is people who have family relations with persons as referred to in number 19 due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, or guardianship who reside in the household, as well as people who work to assist the household and reside in that household.

Article 3
The purpose of protection for women and children victims of acts of violence is to provide protection and services in the best interests of victims of acts of violence that occur in the household and/or in public.

Article 15
The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 42
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government.

Article 17
In implementing efforts to prevent acts of violence against women and children, the Regional Government must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

However, the text does not explicitly mention “perbudakan seksual” (sexual slavery) or “eksploitasi seksual” as a distinct form, nor does it clearly equate trafficking with sexual exploitation/slavery. Given only the retrieved English passages (Articles 7 and 9), a ‘No’ is a reasonable, text-faithful answer for an indicator specifically about sexual slavery/exploitation. This suggests the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-interprets the presence of trafficking/commercial sexual coercion as automatically satisfying sexual slavery/exploitation.
